newsitem.title: UK: Indian GDRs end little changed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian GDRs end little changed in thin trade.

text.p: Indian Global Depositary Receipts were little changed in low volume trade on Monday, hit by the closure of the U.S. markets, dealers said.
"The demand remained low, no one particularly followed the gains on the local market," a dealer said.
The Cazenove Indian GDR index closed marginally higher at 79.78 while the local Bombay Stock Exchange Index rose 58.30 points at 3,580.29.
"Its been very quiet, no one wants to buy further into a rising (local) market. In fact you could see some profit booking in the next few days," another dealer said.
Dealers forecast light trade for the next few days ahead of a Indian central budget due on February 28.
"Before that (the budget) there will be very little economic information that could drive up shares," a trader said.
Political tension between North and South Korea had a dampening effect on demand for Korean shares.
The Capel Korea index was down 2.71 points at 64.31 while the Capel Taiwan index edged ahead by 1.01 points to 102.03.
